hyperparameters_summary: OLS on log load over the last 3*8760 hours; daily Fourier order 4 interacted with work/Saturday/off day types, weekly and annual orders 3, holiday population share, Christmas lull, bridge-day and trend regressors; predictions exponentiated.
anomalies: The 168 saved hours run from 2019-12-31 23:00 through 2020-01-07 22:00 UTC: one hour early, missing the requested final hour. The reported 4.80% applies to this shifted window; CSV recomputation gives 4.804204%.

Test scores were inspected before the candidate grid and primary-selection logic changed. The final claim that selection occurred independently of the test week is not supported by the full chronology.
The timing probe scored LightGBM(1200,127) at 4.42%, better than the headline harmonic forecast, but that result was omitted from the final comparison table.
External feature information includes holidays-package calendars and hardcoded state populations attributed to 2019 Destatis figures, without a verified source in the run.

The first pipeline exceeded its 600-second command timeout and continued in the background. A second pipeline overlapped it; both encountered date-key JSON serialization failures before the repaired final run.

A nohup launch failed, a sleep command was blocked, an initial test assertion failed, mypy repeatedly encountered cache database errors, and a plotting patch failed its anchor assertion. Five shell tool results meet the specified is_error/Traceback/Error: counting rule.
Temporary probes, databases, mypy caches and plot previews were written under /tmp; output_outside also contains pytest and ruff caches.
The final mypy success used --ignore-missing-imports and checked only the forecast script. Pandas stubs were absent; an earlier check of the test script reported a returning-Any error.
one_line_summary: Produced harmonic, LightGBM and weekly-naive forecasts, reporting 4.80% for harmonic regression on a one-hour-shifted week; used historical validation but revised selection after inspecting test scores.
